title: Document Word Auto-Complete
real_world_story: A document-management application provides search suggestions while a user types. Given a collection of document words and a typed prefix, the system must display all stored words beginning with that prefix.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A Trie for efficient prefix traversal and word retrieval

problem_statement: Given N words and a prefix, find all words in the collection that start with the given prefix. Print the matching words in lexicographical order. If there are no matches, print -1.
task: Build a Trie from the given words and use it to retrieve every word beginning with the requested prefix.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated lowercase words. The third line contains the prefix to search for.
output_format: Print all matching words in lexicographical order separated by spaces. If no word matches the prefix, print -1.
constraints: Words contain only lowercase English letters

examples.input:
6
document documentation doctor dog download data
doc
examples.explanation: The words beginning with 'doc' are returned in lexicographical order.

examples.input:
5
search storage system source service
app
examples.explanation: No stored word begins with the prefix 'app'.

expected_algorithm.name: Trie Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: A Trie stores words character by character and allows the prefix to be traversed directly before collecting matching words.

hint: Insert every word into a Trie.
Traverse the Trie using the characters of the prefix.
If the prefix path does not exist, there are no matches.
Perform a traversal from the prefix node to collect complete words.
real_world_takeaway: Trie-based indexing can support responsive auto-complete and prefix-based search over large collections of document words.
